universal_lens: The structural unification of tauopathy progression is modeled as a non-linear dynamical system where the accumulation of truncated tau fragments acts as a bifurcation parameter. This induces a phase transition in lipidomic manifolds, shifting the metabolic state from homeostatic equilibrium to an inflammatory attractor prior to macroscopic neurofibrillary tangle formation.
gsi_mapping: GSI maps the longitudinal metabolomic time-series (4-14 months) using conformal inference to establish dynamic prediction intervals for lipid deregulation. The engine evaluates counterfactual lipidomic trajectories to identify critical intervention windows before irreversible membrane reorganization and neuronal cell death occur.

The introduction of truncated tau fragments (aa151-391/3R) introduces a time-dependent perturbation V'(t), fundamentally altering the energy landscape. We observe that this perturbation does not immediately cause macroscopic structural failure (neurofibrillary tangles). Instead, it triggers a subtle but profound shift in the eigenvalues of the lipidomic covariance matrix. This implies a hidden Markov structure in disease progression, where lipid deregulation is the latent state driving observable cognitive decline. The 'gliotrophic_inflammation_flux' operator quantifies the coupling strength between neuronal tau burden and glial activation, effectively modeling the system as a set of coupled oscillators falling out of sync. The failure mode of current therapeutic strategies is their focus on A_{HMW} rather than stabilizing the underlying metabolic manifold.

reasoning_traces.retrocausal_genealogy: This framework extends classical thermodynamic models of protein misfolding, pioneered by Anfinsen and later adapted for amyloidogenesis by Eisenberg. It borrows heavily from Waddington's epigenetic landscape theory, reinterpreting metabolic valleys as attractors in a dissipative biological system. Furthermore, it aligns with modern network medicine approaches, treating lipid deregulation not as a downstream consequence, but as a primary driver retroactively influencing tau conformational stability through altered membrane biophysics.
reasoning_traces.theory_of_mind: We model the opposing agents as the homeostatic machinery of astrocytes attempting to buffer toxic tau species versus the self-perpetuating feedback loop of microglial activation. The astrocytic agent aims to minimize the inflammatory flux \Phi_{inf}, while the pathological tau exerts a coercive pressure forcing membrane reorganization. The decision actor—the host organism—is trapped in a suboptimal local minimum where energy metabolism declines as resources are diverted to futile inflammatory responses, ultimately leading to systemic neuronal cell death.
